As of last night, I have played every Hero in the game at least twice (I think; once for absolutely sure, but if there's a hero I failed to play a second time I can't think of it), and so I have a pretty good grasp of their playstyles, though I may have missed a few nuances.  I thought it would be interesting to sit down and try to figure out, of all 18 heroes, which ones do I like the most and the least.  It's a difficult analysis for me to perform, which is probably why I'm doing it; nearly every character has some things I like and some things I don't, so I'll play them all with relatively little prejudice, but overall, I've got some overall preferences, and will attempt to narrow them down to an exact numerical ranking.

Top Third

* Nightmist.  I was inclined to give her the top spot after my first time playing her, but I got in another game before I made up my mind.  That game confirmed that it's not as total a preference as I might have thought…I rather like the element of resource management and tricky redirection that she relies upon, but sometimes the awkwardness and fiddlyness can get to me.  Having to constantly check the spell-power of cards in order to determine what she'll do is something of a nuisance, and the fact that she can't do virtually anything when out of cards or low on HP is a serious problem; I can see a lot of potential for her to be frustrating.  Also in both of my games with her, I got the Amulet of the Elder Gods on turn 1, and I can see that she's probably a lot harder to have a satisfying game with if you fail to obtain that.  Still, overall, I have come to regard her as having the most mechanical depth, the most enjoyable diversity of options, and the coolest overall flavor.  She's not somebody I'll always be in the mood for, but I feel like it's going to be a very long time before I've fully plumbed the depths of what she's capable of (not least because I don't own her, and thus can't play endless solitaire games with her as I can with Scholar, Chrono and Zero), and thus I won't be growing contemptuously familiar with her anytime soon.

* Scholar.  I love the character concept (in part because he reminds me of my best friend, an amiable old hippie who agrees that The Scholar is pretty much himself in game form), and the mechanical complexity he offers is highly satisfying to me.  I'm currently estimating him at #2 on my list because of how underwhelming he can be in the early game, with only 1 or 2 cards out and possibly no use for his Power, and because there's often a bit of awkwardness with getting him set up.  He seems to be the most "quadratic" of all characters, with his power level starting out at a very shallow curve and then abruptly spiking into the stratosphere, and I approve of that less than I do with a steady diagonal buildup.  It can also be a problem when he's at full health and unable to regain more, which prevents him from triggering Mortal Form to Energy to deal out damage.  Still, he does a lot of things I really enjoy (drawing cards, healing, resisting damage, hitting multiple targets, and chaining combos), and the bottom line is I have a lot of fun with him, at least when things aren't going horribly wrong - I've got him ranked below Nightmist at least in part because, with her, you sort of expect that things will go horribly wrong and are mentally prepared for it, whereas with scholar, you kind of actively something screwing you up just when you've finally got all the pieces put together.

* Tachyon.  Was my first favorite from about the third game I played, and has largely retained that status.  I'm just beginning to get a little bored with her simplicity, but her ability to play multiple cards and sometimes to get insanely large effects out of them remain highly satisfying to me.  Playing her feels like a game of pinball - you have to think a little but not too hard, and you get a lot of very quick rewards for your effort, but the appeal eventually wears thin.  I have a spectacularly poor win record with her (she's won only 3 out of 7 games where I was present, and in one of those she was more useful dead than alive, while in another she had been completely neutered by the end; the games where I actually play her myself almost always seem to be against the hardest villains, and her low HP means she's usually one of the first to die), but I almost always enjoy myself when playing with her.

* Chrono-Ranger.  Earlier in my time on this forum, someone heard me talking about my preferences in other heroes and suggested that I'd probably enjoy Chrono-Ranger; I can now verify that this person was right.  While my top five characters are practically a tie, I've kind of pushed CR toward the bottom because of his linearity, which is both a strength and a weakness, but overall tends to negatively affect his panache.  (This may change with time, as he's less likely to be completely screwed out of a game than many characters, and thus is less likely to have his rating go down when I'm in a bad mood.)  Nearly always tossing off 1 damage in addition to everything else he does is a good way to stay engaged in the game, but often there are a shortage of useful options for such attacks, and the repetitiveness is a downside as much as the reliability is an upside.  He offers a diversity of options with his equipment and Bounties, which is good; the base experience is very satisfying, and he has a lot of potential to skyrocket in power if things go right, while he's less sensitive than most heroes to them going wrong.  Overall, a very well-rounded, strong and enjoyable hero, but the flavor isn't ideal for me and he's a bit simpler than other highly-involved heroes, so I don't feel that he quite takes the top spot.

* Absolute Zero.  I've debated ranking AZ above Tachyon before, but for now have decided against it, since he has more potential to go awry and be left stuck without good options.  Even so, I love the combo-centricity of the character, as well as his disgruntled and sarcastic attitude, and the way his effectiveness varies wildly in different Environments.  He has a lot of cards which can end up being duds depending on the situation, and that can be frustrating, but overall I find him very engaging most of the time.

* Expatriette.  I'm not into guns at all, and so from a flavor perspective, Expat is an absolute bletch to me.  But mechanically, I find her very satisfying.  The Ammo cards are often useless, and getting a Gun into play is often much harder than it should be, but when she works, she really works, and I find the array of options she offers very enticing.  She's kind of my own personal dark horse, the character I didn't expect to like, yet somehow do.

Middle Third

* Omnitron-X.  This character has the potential to end up in the top third instead, but he's got an awkwardness and repetitiveness that I feel keeps him from cracking that for now.  Too many of his cards are Components that blow up when he's walloped, too many of his options involve discarding or destroying his own cards, the Plating mechanic is somewhat annoying, and I often fail to find good targets for Bio-Engineering Beam.  Interestingly, I have never used Reset in either of the games I've played with him, but it's not likely to improve his ranking when I do, as I consider extraneous shuffling to be a nuisance, and not entirely beneficial anyway.  The extreme narrowness of Defensive Blast, offset by its ridiculous potency when it works, is a sore spot to me; I don't tend to like characters that are too swingy, with too much potential to take over the game or to fall flat.  Note that Omnitron is very high in my rankings in spite of all these failings; the Timeshift power alone is pure awesomeness, and he gets to play still more extra cards with Slip Through Time and Electro-Deployment Unit, so he's front-loaded with a lot of things I love…he just also has a lot of ways to screw up, and as a result ends up being a highly conditional fave.

* Tempest.  Extremely powerful, but simple enough to make a good starting pick, Tempest is just an all-around solid character, and that's pretty much all I have to say about him.

* Visionary.  She was an early favorite of mine, and I still love her playstyle…but the extent to which she utterly takes over and neuters several matches have left me reluctant to play her again.  Were she more completely about Wrest the Mind, Twist the Ether, and Mental Divergence, she'd be an absolute, no-qualifications favorite of mine, but as it stands, her Enlighten power means that she spends a lot of time churning through her deck, and sooner or later comes upon Precognition and Suggestion, cards which are too powerful not to play, but result in an otherwise-challenging match turning into a cakewalk.  It's rather sad, and it's happened to me too many times, so my original fondness for Visi has been severely tarnished.  (And I have absolutely zero intention of ever playing Dark Visionary, a version which gives up her awesome Enlighten Power in order to become even more thoroughly the part of her that I don't like.)  She also leads to some frustration when I spend too much time drawing her more underwhelming cards, such as Mass Levitation, Mind Spike, Precognitive Vision, or even Foresight (which is better than Enlightening herself, but lacks the ability to help other characters, and overall tends not to seem like the best use of my card play for the turn).

* Unity.  Flavor-wise, I absolutely love her; she's one of my very favorite characters on a strictly conceptual level.  But I'm forced to rank her as low as this because she has TWO of the three things (the third is being flat-out boring, which fortunately doesn't apply to her) which I see as being able to ruin a character: being powerful enough to utterly steam roll a game, and the potential to be completely useless and frustratingly unable to turn things around.  It's very possible for Uni to get a bad draw or be screwed by villain/enviro cards, and be left with two or three Golems in hand and no way of playing them; conversely, if she draws no Golems at all, but just a bunch of Volatile Parts and Powered Shockwaves, she's not getting anywhere either, and can't even cannibalize her allies' Equipment to fix the problem.  (Also, the game is supposed to be co-op, but bot-fix is the kind of power that lets an antisocial player screw his buddies over and sabotage the entire group's chances of winning, just because the player is the kind of person who wants to dominate the game rather than sharing in a collective victory.  Between that risk and the general fact that she's complicated and potentially frustrating, I strongly believe nobody should ever be offered the chance to play Unity until they've played the game several times with more standard characters.)

* Ra.  I don't think I'm exagerrating when I say that Ra is the single simplest, most newbie-friendly character in the game, and as a result, he inevitably becomes a little boring once you've played as often as I have.  But he's very good at what he does, has a surprisingly wide array of ways to do it, and the bottom line is that I love Egyptian stuff, so in spite of his almost insulting straightforwardness, Ra still manages to rank fairly high among my preferences, even though I always try to find other characters I'd rather play before resorting to him.

* Haka.  The very first character I played, he's never really excited me, but I consider him very solid.  His immense HP simply means he stays in the game longer than most, and that alone is an advantage; he also has a built-in damage power, which is something I usually wish I had when playing the more involved heroes.  He draws a ton of extra cards, although I usually find myself playing his Hakas just for card draw because I don't want to discard anything.  It annoys me how powerful the Taiaha is; once that shows up, there's no reason not to use it, but it seems to outshine so many other options that I can't help but feel saddened.  Savage Mana is an absolute spoiler in certain otherwise-difficult matches, and it varies whether I feel that this is a good thing or a bad thing.  Finally, he has a lot of cards that are only useful in certain Environments, and I seem to be extremely good at drawing them when not in such environments.  I consider him a good fallback character, but one I've resorted to too often, and thus I try to find reasons not to play him again, so as not to intensify my feeling of meh-ness.

Lower Third

* Mr. Fixer.  I wanna like this guy, I really do.  But the bottom line is, he seems to be really weak, and I've yet to have a single game where he was able to get both a Style and a Tool in play so he could really go to town.  Usually I draw multiples of one or the other of those things, leaving me with few cards I can actually play, and his little 1-damage plinks are hardly worth bothering to do.  If I recall my rankings correctly, he's the only character who I've played three times and not scored a single victory with.  I find his intricacy conceptually interesting and keep wanting to give him another chance, but I have yet to even start really enjoying myself with him - even when he's almost beginning to work, he's really not that much fun to me, and the bottom line is that fun is what it's all about.

* Wraith.  The very first character I played, she's almost as simple as Ra but has a little more depth, although I don't enjoy her as much on a flavor level.  The effectiveness of Micro-Targeting Computer plus one of her throwing weapons leaves me with little desire to explore the other options she possesses, which is a real pity.  I think the most fun I've ever seen someone have with her was when a Ruins of Atlantis card forced her to play an inconveniently-timed Inventory Barrage and throw away all her stuff for a non-lethal blow to the villain (who was Gloomweaver, so we weren't even supposed to be attacking him anyway, as we were waiting for his third Relic to come out so we could kill that and win).  She has the potential to be fun, but is unlikely to fully utilize it, and so I tend to leave her on the bench these days.

* Bunker.  I started to develop a bit of a fondness for Bunker's mechanical complexity early on, but it faded fast; he's neither a simple character nor an intricate one, but in an unhappy medium where he takes effort to figure out but is quickly solved and left without further depth.  Once you get that it's all about Recharging until you draw the other two Modes, then Upgrading to get down two guns and going Turret for the rest of the game while you fire them, you quickly realize that the entire rest of his deck is irrelevant and you'll never do anything interesting thereafter.  Add that to my lack of personal fondness for the military theme, and I've got very few reasons to like Bunker, though I will occasionally give him another chance to try and impress me.

* Fanatic.  I'm strongly un-fond of her Christian-ness, and while she has a lot of fun cards (I do wish anyone else got something like Final Dive or Embolden), she also has a lot of ways to completely take over the game (I've seen so many villains finished off by Wrathful Retribution or utterly gimped by End of Days; it's long ago stopped being funny).  I like to say that if your idea of "strategy" is to pray for a miracle, Fanatic is your character, and she's very definitely not mine, but I not only don't tend to want to play her, I often would rather she wasn't being played at all, because of how much potential she has to eclipse the contributions of the other heroes.

* Argent Adept.  I saved this character for last to try, because I wasn't interested in his musician-ness and because he was rumored to be fiendishly complicated.  Turns out, he was even MORE complicated than the rumors held, and I don't feel that the complexity pays off with a deserved reward, as is true for Nightmist or Scholar or Zero.  He has a lot of different effects among his music Ongoings, but many of them strike me as relatively weak (healing is nice, but it's only 1 point at a time; card-control is only worthwhile if you'll survive long enough to draw and play the resulting cards, which is less likely since the Adept hasn't done anything to stop the villains while he was setting up your cards, and destroying Ongoing or Environment cards is theoretically a life-saver, but very often there aren't any out which are worth bothering with).  And above all, I find it a nuisance to have to track which ongoings are Melodys, Rhythms or Harmonies (the cardnames don't tend to help much, at least not unless you're a music geek), and which instrument will play which half of which of those card types; it's a lot of hoops to jump through, and only a few of the effects seem to have enough of a payoff to justify that.  Overall, while I'm due to play him a bunch more times and may eventually decide he's somewhat more enjoyable, I currently feel very justified in calling him one of my least favorites - too much effort for too little result, and an unappealing flavor on top of it.

* Legacy.  I wish I could like this guy, since conceptually he appeals to me - as something of a USA Patriot myself, I want to be able to cheer for a character that combines some of the best aspects of Superman and Captain America.  But the fact of the matter is, Legacy's Galvanize power makes him a glorified cheerleader, his deck has an extremely high proportion of situationally-useless cards (Danger Sense, Next Evolution, Lead from the Front, Surge of Strength, Heroic Interception, and even Bolster Allies if the heroes won't survive long enough to play the cards they drew…all of these can fail to be relevant under fairly regular circumstances).  When he's at his absolute best, he can entirely render the hero team invincible (to the best of my knowledge this is only possible in one Environment, but still), which is not necessarily a good thing, since the game is less fun when it entirely ceases to be a challenge.  It's nice to have Legacy in your game, but I don't want to be the one who's stuck having to play him; his simplicity and "buddy-buddyness" makes him a great choice for new players, and I of course have long since stopped being one of those, so now I am quite confident in saying that Legacy is the character I least wish to play ever again.

* Argent Adept.  I saved this character for last to try, because I wasn't interested in his musician-ness and because he was rumored to be fiendishly complicated.  Turns out, he was even MORE complicated than the rumors held, and I don't feel that the complexity pays off with a deserved reward, as is true for Nightmist or Scholar or Zero.  He has a lot of different effects among his music Ongoings, but many of them strike me as relatively weak (healing is nice, but it's only 1 point at a time; card-control is only worthwhile if you'll survive long enough to draw and play the resulting cards, which is less likely since the Adept hasn't done anything to stop the villains while he was setting up your cards, and destroying Ongoing or Environment cards is theoretically a life-saver, but very often there aren't any out which are worth bothering with).  And above all, I find it a nuisance to have to track which ongoings are Melodys, Rhythms or Harmonies (the cardnames don't tend to help much, at least not unless you're a music geek), and which instrument will play which half of which of those card types; it's a lot of hoops to jump through, and only a few of the effects seem to have enough of a payoff to justify that.  Overall, while I'm due to play him a bunch more times and may eventually decide he's somewhat more enjoyable, I currently feel very justified in calling him one of my least favorites - too much effort for too little result, and an unappealing flavor on top of it.

* Legacy.  I wish I could like this guy, since conceptually he appeals to me - as something of a USA Patriot myself, I want to be able to cheer for a character that combines some of the best aspects of Superman and Captain America.  But the fact of the matter is, Legacy's Galvanize power makes him a glorified cheerleader, his deck has an extremely high proportion of situationally-useless cards (Danger Sense, Next Evolution, Lead from the Front, Surge of Strength, Heroic Interception, and even Bolster Allies if the heroes won't survive long enough to play the cards they drew...all of these can fail to be relevant under fairly regular circumstances).  When he's at his absolute best, he can entirely render the hero team invincible (to the best of my knowledge this is only possible in one Environment, but still), which is not necessarily a good thing, since the game is less fun when it entirely ceases to be a challenge.  It's nice to have Legacy in your game, but I don't want to be the one who's stuck having to play him; his simplicity and "buddy-buddyness" makes him a great choice for new players, and I of course have long since stopped being one of those, so now I am quite confident in saying that Legacy is the character I least wish to play ever again.

I take slight issue with the "Adept can't do anything at all unless her has a card in play" thing. Um. Arcane Cadence? Vernal Sonata? He can't do anything in his Power phase unless he has a song in play, but that's not the same thing - if your Play phase can't get you a song in the first turn, then yeah, you skip your Power phase for that round, but he has so many songs in his deck and four (I think) copies of Arcane Cadence that the chances of you obtaining a song, any song in the first turn and getting it out are pretty high! posts.name: PlatinumWarlock
posts.cooked:
First impressions are one thing, but I find that some heroes grow on you, the more you play them.  Argent Adept was like that for me.  The last game that I played as him, I ended up being able to chain together two instruments, letting everyone heal for 2 (or heal for 1 and destroy an environment/ongoing) and let someone else at the table either draw or play a card....all on my Power phase.    

What's especially neat to me is when you get heroes chaining together to do really awesome stuff or to try out new ways to play..  Our group had Scholar, Tempest and AA working together to churn through trash piles:  we played "Don't Dismiss Anything" five times in the same game, which really fueled some butt-kicking for us!  Plus, because I was healing 2 hp most rounds, The Scholar became my personal cannon, via Mortal Form to Energy.  One hero in a vacuum might not be impressive, but when you start working them together, the sum is greater than the parts.

Similarly, in one of the forum games recently, I watched someone play Visionary in a way that I'd never seen before, using Wrest the Mind to take out minion after minion with no backlash.  In another online game, I saw someone play Fanatic in a way that I'd never contemplated before, using Sacrosanct Martyr in ways that I'd simply never done.  I've seen Mister Fixer pull off stuff that's simply unbelievable, comboing redirected damage from allies and himself to outright lay out foes.  Individually, you wouldn't necessarily see these interactions, but they come up in the context of other characters, they're great!

I guess the key in a lot of ways is to keep an open mind when playing.  The biggest value in SotM for me is its replay value and that's exemplified by the sheer number of ways each hero can be played.  Don't be afraid to be surprised!

posts.cooked:
Envisioner, everything seems to keep getting put into either being too weak or overpowered.

Some heroes are intended to be stronger than others, the balance of the game is intended towards team balancing.

The moments where a hero really carries the day isn't bad game mechanics, its the way the game was intended.  Your hero doesn't always get to be the one that shines, but sometimes your hero is the one that saves everybody and turns the fight against the villain.  It is a comic Book themed game, it should work that way.

Every once in a while enough of the team click that the villain just gets wiped out with no real threat to the heroes.  There are always fights where it is too easy, usually because there is something really nasty on the horizon.

I don't mind those fights, or the ones where you get creamed and it never at any point felt like you had a chance to win, because those are proper Comic Book fights as well.  The heroes don't always know why they won so easily or lost so badly, the bigger picture isn't complete.  I love the revenge matches, and the "Seriously Omnitron, how many times do we have to beat you down?" sequences as well.

This is one of the reasons I've gotten into modding the Villains, esp. adding the lieutenants to them, Omnitron is going to upgrade himself if he keeps failing to destroy the heroes, and the next time the cultists try to sommon Gloomweaver they might make sure they have a little extra help doing so.

Eventually you have a fight that settles a story line, and you get to start a new one.  That's what I love about Sentinels, we are telling a comic book story everytime we fight, we just don't know if it is a one-shot, or part of a bigger arc until the fight is over.

I don't know what Vernal Sonata is, but I'll grant you Arcane Cadence, that's a very strong card and having it in your opening hand (or after losing all your stuff) makes a big difference.  But it's just one card with 2-4 copies in deck, so you have a 5-10% chance of having it; the rest of the time, you're probably playing a card, activating it, and quite possibly losing it to villain/enviro destruction, so next turn you get to do it again.  You can't normally activate Accompany texts until you start the turn with that card in play, and the Instruments do nothing without a song in play, so you always have to play a song first, and then hope it survives until you can play the Instrument which will play both halves of it - assuming you even can do an entire card with one instrument (I saw this being possible for Xu's Bell, but the other two instruments I saw required two different cards to activate fully).  It might not be quite as fragile as Mr. Fixer, and it probably pays off better if you can survive, but it definitely seems like a strategy that's highly vulnerable to interference.

Rabit:

Visionary (Envisioner: Ever use her base power to help someone else?)

Yes of course; I usually try to target someone downstream from her in turn order, so that they can play the resulting card without waiting for the next turn.  Besides, other characters are seemingly more likely to have duplicate Limited cards (even when Visi's cards are Limited, they're often things like Wrest the Mind which destroy themselves after use, versus Haka's Ta Moko and Taiaha for example), so even targeting someone upstream of Visi is often better than targeting herself.  I mentioned when I was analyzing Visionary that Foresight was often one of her less strong options, because while it gives better card access than Enlighten, it can't target others.

(Envisioner: The fact you think you've solved him is highly entertaining to me, as what you described is far from the "best" way to play him. )

It is pretty much the best when your objective is to deal a lot of damage to the villain, which is of course not always the case.  But if you do want to deal damage, your only other real option is the Omni-Cannon, which is vulnerable enough to destruction that it likely may not be worth depleting your card supply for.

The message I was really trying to get across in my earlier post was not to discount a hero because you had two poor games with them.

Nowhere have I done that.  My reasons for disliking Argent Adept were not based primarily on his poor performance, but on the fact that he's excessively fiddly to play, and thematically unsatisfying to me personally.  Fixer I am kind of down on based on his poor performance, but that's in three games, during which I've seen most of his cards.  Driving Mantis style can be very nice in certain matchups, Grease Gun is a lifesaver, Dual Crowbars are very nice, and Scrap Yard is huge, but overall he just doesn't have much gas compared to other heroes; he has to keep an Ongoing and an Equipment in play in order for Harmony to do anything at all, and his innate power deals less damage than other heroes who have a built-in attack, except for Chrono-Ranger who does extra damage on nearly every card he plays.  Like I said, I want to like Fixer; as a character, he's very cool, and somehow the hoops you have to jump through getting him to work are satisfying to me…but he really doesn't give you enough of a payoff for them, so playing him is kind of a masochistic experience.  I think there are a few minor tweaks that could have made all the difference for him, such as making his Strike deal irreducible damage right off the bat, and replacing one of the two irreducible-based styles with something more proactive.  As it stands, he has a lot of dead cards in any match where the villain doesn't rely on reductions, and when the villain does, he still has an uphill battle getting the right Style and keeping it in play.

Sure, enjoy the heroes you're enjoying now, but after a while dip back into the pool and see what you think about the other heroes now that you have a better understanding of the game.

I plan on it.  Although I'm going to be staying away from Fanatic for a very long time, after the TWO games she utterly punked with turn 1 End of Days, and the several times that she's Wrathful Retributionned for the win.  Heck, I might just take those cards out of her deck and see how playable she is then.

Some folks don't like taking on a support role with heroes like Legacy and Visionary, but that's what those heroes do.

Legacy that's true of for sure, but Visionary to me is more about battlefield control.  Mental Divergence looping Wrest the Mind, or repeated Precogs and Suggestions…these seem to be at least as effective as feeding your teammates cards, though of course it will all depend on the situation.

(or they come up with home rules that alter the heroes to make them the way they want them)!

I'm generally somewhat reluctant to houserule the game, as it complicates the process of introducing new players, wonks with game balance, and generally increases mental bookkeeping.  I have yet to actually institute any house rules, and have only even begun to think about a few of them.

Vernal Sonata - One-shot. Heals all hero targets for 1hp and then all heroes can choose one card from their trash (not Vernal Sonata) and put it on top of their deck.

The Adept can suffer if someone destroys his stuff, yes, but so can anyone else. And with the Adept, it can be pretty easy to cycle through his deck, especially in a long game. I've had my entire deck out before (a mixture of cards being in-hand or in play), which was cool. Arcane Cadence is good for getting cards out in the early game so I tend to use it ASAP if I start with it (and frequently chain into a second, or more), then later not really use it so much but give Silver Shadow more attention.

As far as I can remember, there are three different Harmonies, Melodies, and Rhythms. That's nine cards. But there are two of each, so that's eighteen cards, just under half the deck. Then you have four copies of Arcane Cadence. Even if you start with no songs in-hand but one copy of Arcane Cadence, it's almost like being able to start with a hand of nine cards but then having to stick some of them in other places (trash, top of deck, bottom of deck).

My style of playing the Adept involves playing Arcane Cadence if I get it in my starting hand, chaining into other copies of the card if I reveal them as a result of using that first copy (should I reveal two copies with one card, I can put one on top of the deck so it comes out when I play the other one). After all this is done, all I need to do is make sure that among the cards revealed by the final Cadence, one of them is a song and goes into play. Then I have something to do with my Power phase. I don't always remember this and end up playing something else and then going "Oops, I forgot, now I don't have a power I can use - oh well", but that's just me being forgetful and it doesn't usually make too much of a difference. If one of my songs/instruments gets destroyed, I have Vernal Sonata and Instrumental Conjuration to get stuff back. The latter also lets me draw a card, which is a nice bonus.

Once I get set up with a nice selection of stuff, I can potentially, in my Power phase, let myself use another power, which I use to let myself use another power (Harp + Lyra + Inspiring Supertonic, wheeee :D), which I use to let myself or someone else do a wide variety of possible different things. I can play or draw a card, or let someone else do that. I can give up to two hero targets +1 damage and/or +1 soak. I can ditch one of my instruments to insta-kill absolutely anything in play that isn't indestructible or a character card (aww Voss, did you like that spaceship? Or Apostate, were you counting on the soak from those Runes protecting your stuff? Shame >:)). I can heal myself for up to 4hp, and everyone else for up to 2hp. I can destroy up to two ongoing/environment cards. I can do some other stuff that I can't remember right now. And that's just the Power phase. Never mind that I might have used a song effect in my Play phase via Silver Shadow...multiple times, if I have more than one copy of that particular card. Oh yeah, and if someone else happens to be able to let me use a power on their turn...wheee, here we go again!

The Adept might stat with the lowest hp total of any hero, but he makes up for it by being, as far as I can see, one of the most versatile. The fact that you can use the same song effects multiple times (Perform and Accompany texts aren't powers, remember, so there's no limit on how often you can use them in your turn, provided you have the means to do so) can just get insane :D.

Wow, what's the reverse of a rant? I think I just managed it - sorry ;).

On the subject of Bunker, another set-up for him can be Heavy Plating, Recharge Mode, and the Omni-Cannon. Then you get to draw three cards a turn and have pretty good soak so can tank a lot while you charge up your Omni-Cannon. Basically, every hero has their strengths and weaknesses. Some will get their arses totally kicked in some circumstances whilst seeming almost obscenely overpowered in others. That's just the way it goes, and is kind of the point of the game - it encourages the players to think about what they're doing and plan their tactics together and stuff. If one hero is having trouble right now (say, Jim or Tachyon because the villain has a pint or two of soak), then another can help them out (maybe Legacy can buff their damage, Mr Fixer with his Riveting Crane and self-buffs can get through the soak and remove it for everyone else, etc). * I've played Haka five times, but only against three different villains - Baron Blade and Grand Warlord Voss on both regular and advanced, plus the Dreamer on regular.  Conversely, in six games Absolute Zero, Bunker, and Ra have never repeated a villain.

* I've played Chrono-Ranger in only three different Environments: Silver Gulch, the Final Wasteland, and once on Mars.  Bunker, Legacy and the Scholar have managed never to visit the same Environment twice.

* After five games each, Unity and Visionary have never been incapacitated.  (Granted the same was true of the Scholar until he played his sixth game...but he only died there because I royally screwed up, so I have every reason to expect that U&V will go 6-0.)  In the same number of games, I've gotten Fanatic killed four times and lost the whole game three of them.  Tachyon and Zero have also died four times, but that was in six games, and they won all but two of them.

* I have never played Absolute Zero second in turn order.  Bunker and Tempest have never gone fourth, and none of Chrono-Ranger, Tachyon or The Scholar have ever been third,   Not one hero has managed to play a different position (out of the twelve possible ones) in each of six games.

posts.cooked:
Have gotten enough additional experience playing each hero (except Nightmist, who I don't think I've upticked since making this list - she's at 3 games right now, while everyone else is at least 5 and some are as high as 8) that I'm revising the order a bit, as well as further subcategorizing into six tiers rather than three.

Tier 1 - All-Time Faves

* Scholar.  While occasionally awkward, his playstyle is rewarding to me on so many levels, and I just love the flavor of him.  There may not be a more fun or much-more powerful card in the game than Proverbs and Axioms, and I love the numerical minigame of figuring out how best to use "Get Out of the Way!".

* Chrono-Ranger.  I concede the point to whoever said before I'd really enjoy CR, because I really do.  Probably the only reason I don't put him at #1 is that he lacks a lot of effectiveness when he can't get a Bounty out early on.

* Nightmist.  I've decided that too many of the decisions she forces you to make are painful for me to call her my #1 hero anymore.  But she's still incredibly interesting to me.

Tier 2 - Excellent Fun

* Absolute Zero.  The high-risk high-reward nature appeals to me less than simply the fact that he has to jump through a few hoops to become effective; he's the simplest of the Complexity 3 heroes, and that puts him at a sort of sweet spot.  Also I love his personality, though some of his flavor text isn't ideal to me.

* Omnitron-X.  I love the complicated, builduppy heroes with nuclear potential, and I've had some spectacular Omnitron games which have made him shoot upward in the rankings.  He's not higher than he is because of a certain level of clunkiness he suffers, the general shortage of one-shots other than Reset, the multiple reshuffles that one forces, the brokenness of Bio-Engineering Beam which turns awesome cards like Anubis into lame anticlimaxes, the fact that Timeshift stops short of some of its ideally desireable applications by being unable to return the card to the top of the deck, and the mechanical silliness of being able to destroy other heroes' Equipment and even Omnitron's Components for Singularity and Self-Sabotage.  Lots of individual negatives, but the whole they assemble into is cool enough that they can largely be forgiven.

* Tachyon.  Still appeals to my more ADD tendencies.  She's just fun, has some of the most powerful cards, is easy to understand but full of nuances, and is a hilarious character.

Tier 3 - Highly Enjoyable

* Visionary. Still the intellectual, megalomaniacal heroine I love, with a lot of really cool cards that nobody else really duplicates.  I still dislike how badly she can gimp certain villains with Precognition and Suggestion (and for this reason, Dark Visi is absolutely the last of the promo heroes I will ever want to play), and her psychic damage one-shots are also underwhelming, so she's swingier than I wish she were and often fails to live up to her potential.  But just her build-in power automatically goes some distance to correct this shortcoming, as well as making her a great team enabler.  As long as I stay away from the matchups which prime her to be stupidly overpowered in a lame way, and concentrate on giving her opportunities to shine in a unique and satisfying way, she'll bring me much joy.

* Expatriette.  Not much to say beyond what I've already said.  I have had a game with her since my previous writing where she opened on a hand with three Ammo and no Guns, and that royally sucked.  Speed Loading should really be at least a 3x in her deck, more Arsenal Access would be nice, and the fact that there are more Quick Draws than cards to fetch with them is unfortunate, leading to late-game dead draws.  But she's still an enjoyably active character; I feel as if she was a prototype for Chrono-Ranger, and that he profits from the learning experience represented by her shortcomings.  I also love the backstory of her being an exile from the Citizens of the Sun who now plans to prove the deadliness of powerless humanity to her mother; that's great storytelling.

* Tempest.  So powerful, and with loads of options.  I recently pegged him as the one hero I would play exclusively if forced to do so, just because he is better-rounded than my other faves, with his only real weakness being low HP that keeps his bad games mercifully short.  His backstory is a little bland for me and some of his cards are a bit simplistic, but overall he's just extremely solid, and much harder to go wrong with than most heroes, which is a huge plus for me given my dread of bad shuffles.

Tier 4 - Somewhat Conditional Faves

* Ra.  Playing him more, I've found him to contain a satisfying number of additional nuances which help mollify his overall one-noteness, and so I don't feel so bad about resorting to him now and again, even though I always look for reasons to play a more sophisticated hero.

* Unity.  Still a great character whose shtick is theoretically cool, but hampered by fragility and an over-reliance on either luck or exploits, tending to succeed big or fail miserably with little middle ground.  Utterly failed in a recent outing against Iron Legacy, so I've got more of a sour taste for her than usual just at the moment.

* Haka.  I love love love the immense starting HP, and loading up on cards with Mere or Dominion is really fun.  The Hakas are his weak point, as I'm seldom impressed with the healing of Restoration and almost never want to bother with Shielding (though I really must remember to try him against Omnitron sometime, just in the hopes of having him Shield for 16 right before an Electro-Pulse Explosive goes off).  I also generally feel bad about drawing Elbow Smash, as it's just rather underwhelming compared to other cards.  And the whole Maori shtick doesn't do it for me, making much of his flavor text feel wasted...I'd rather hear more about how he adapts to life in the Western world (the general impression I get is "very well", but some more details about how he ended up teaching kindergarden etc. would be nice to have).

Tier 5 - Heroes I Find Lacking Somehow

* Wraith.  Has more depth than I've given her credit for, but not much more; it's often hard to find time to play around with an Infrared Eyepiece or Smoke Bombs when you could just blast for 8 with a Targeting Utility Throwing Razor setup.  Also, her Stealth power goes to waste with tragic frequency; she'll probably be the first hero for whom I try one of the alternate promos.  Still, a very good newbie hero that I still have a soft spot for.

* Mr. Fixer. He's actually trending up rather well compared to my previous games, just not well enough to gain ground as other heroes also uptick.  The asymmetry between his Tools and Styles continues to bug me, as I draw the latter more than the former with truly absurd regularity, and I still tend to find him high-investment-for-medium-reward, similar to the Argent Adept in that regard, but less interesting about it.  However, he remains effective enough, and just at the right balance point between straightforwardness and complexity, for me to still appreciate him.

* Bunker.  As with Wraith, he suffers from the fact that some of his least interesting options are too effective not to emphasize, at the expense of his more clever potential.  And I really wish he had more HP and more soak, in order to qualify for the sobriquet "The Indestructible".  Still, he's one of the heroes I anticipate the most improvement to in future games; he could end up in Tier 3 one day if I grow tired of Expat and Haka and so forth, as he has an amount of depth which they tend to lack.

Tier Six - Played Grudgingly For the Sake of Balance

* Argent Adept.  I've come to understand him more or less fully by now, and this has greatly improved my fondness for him, but not greatly enough to escape the bottom sixth (once the game contains KNYFE and possibly Parse, we'll talk; both of those, from what little we know about them, have the potential to disinterest me).  He's extremely draw-dependent; I've had the "Arcane Cadence into Arcane Cadence" opening now, and it makes so huge a difference in his effectiveness as to leave me incredibly ennoyed he isn't guaranteed to get one in his starting hand.  Inspiring Supertonic is also an absurdly swingy card that gives his games a sea-change of effectiveness depending on whether or not it appears; overall, he's far too variable for my taste, and I still think is maximum potential is nowhere near as impressive as, say, Zero's or Haka's.  But he will likely continue to climb steadily in my esteem, even if he may never gain the momentum to exceed most other heroes.

* Fanatic.  Despite the whole Christian angle, I really want to like her.  Final Dive is one of the greatest cards ever, and the Divine Focus through Prayer of Desperation loop is magnificent...when I manage to play these cards in a game, I tend to enjoy her.  But she still has too many lame incremental one-shots like Brutal Censure, too many game-ending wrecking balls like End of Days and Wrathful Retribution (even as a singleton, that one nearly always seems to come up), and overall too little consistency to be worth putting up with her foibles.

* Legacy.  Still a dull cheerleader of a hero whose contributions to the game are seldom proactive enough for me (Take Down and Lead From The Front are great cards, but passively great, and that's not how I roll).  I like him best as a tank, but too many of his cards are situational at best, and his deck utterly fails as a Superman homage IMO, despite being a flavorfully interesting take on the concept.  I really need to try Young Legacy sometime, as she'll almost definitely be more my style, and Greatest Legacy might be even better, but the original is definitely just about played out for me.

Ameena:

I'm not too sure I'd ever refer to Megalopolis as "newbie-friendly", what with those Hostage Situations, Papparazzi, and Traffic Pile-Ups…

Those are actually a point in favor of the newbies understanding the game (not necessarily winning it, of course, although an easy villain on non-Advanced typically makes that probable anyway).  By skipping a phase, they briefly avoid the cognitive load associated with playing that phase; one of the best ways to speed up the learning process is to decrease the number of decision trees that must be mastered at one time.  And skipping a draw phase means being exposed to fewer new cards (though not none; you'll still see a new villain card for instance), so that also diminishes the learning curve.  But the ultimate trump card in Megalopolis's favor is Rooftop Combat, since it basically turns the Environment deck off altogether, possibly for several turns, and thus reduces the distraction of having to pay attention to more than just the villain.  Once the players are experienced, Megalopolis begins to be boring and frustrating, but to the newbie, it's the best Environment for simplifying the choices they must face in ignorance, letting them concentrate on mastering the new concepts one or two at a time.

(Of course, ease of play is only a point in favor of a newbie game; raw cool factor is another one, and so I might well use Insula Primalis for a newbie environment; everybody loves lava and dinosaurs.)

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Rooftop Combat is certainly a (usually) helpful card due to its shutdown of the environment deck, provided the villain doesn't have so many damaging cards out that the damage bonus doesn't add up to something tremendous. Once we had it come up in the first round against the Dreamer, which was just epic as it meant we had a damage bonus to kill all the projections and could completely ignore the environment deck for the entire game :D.

Personally I would say that having to skip certain phases (which would keep changing as you get rid of one card only for a different one to come up and make you skip something else instead) would probably be confusing, especially for someone who hadn't had enough time to learn the turn phases just yet. I'd prefer to learn what it was I could do and get the hang of it before something started teling me I couldn't do one or more of the things. Still, people differ, so I'm sure there are those who wouldn't be too bothered by it…though there is the other matter of that having to keep skipping phases (if you keep drawing those kind of cards round after round so there's always something you can't do) is basically giving the villain a huge advantage and a game you might otherwise have won without too much trouble can become a rather swift and horrible wipe due to the fact that you couldn't get yourselves going enough to take down whatever the villain is putting out. I've had this happen in games and I reckon it'd be really frustrating to a new player - "Okay so you're playing Ra because he's pretty straightforward and just nukes stuff…except on this turn you can't play any cards so you can't put out that lovely Staff of his…okay, this round you now can't use any base powers so you can't use your now-boosted Pyre skill…and now you can't draw cards so that Living Conflagration is actually now worse than your base power…" and so on. Worse if multiple you-can't-do-that-thing cards are out at once, but hopefully if you're showing a newbie the game you're not going up against someone like the Chairman where that's more likely to happen ;).

My newbie environment of choice is Insula Primalis. Did it on Monday, in fact, when showing a friend the game for the first time. Baron Blade in Insula Primalis. I playe as Legacy and Visionary, so as to give damage buffs (and explain the Nemesis mechanic) and keep Blade's deck under control (good thing I did - the remaining two Mobile Defence Platforms were right next to each other within a couple of cards of the top) without ending up doing loads of damage and risking "taking over" the game. I gave Ra to my friend because as mentioned above, I find him straightforward and you can do All of the Things (ie benefit via both one-shots and ongoings, plus you even have one equipment card) whilst nuking the crap out of everything :). By the end of the (victorious) game Ra was buffed by Galvanise, Inspiring Presence, Imbued Fire, and two Obsidian Fields. He didn't manage to get the Staff out (though had a Summon Staff but didn't get a chance to use it before the game ended), but as he was already doing eight damage with his Blazing Inferno this didn't matter hugely, considering who we were fighting :). We then fought Ambuscade with different heroes and thrashed him too - I could have got the killing blow but I let my friend do it and he strung a load of cards together (was playing TLT though used Research Grant rather than the base power for every round except one) to take out pretty much all the environment targets before finishing off Ambuscade himself. And he's coming round in a couple of hours to play some more :).

If I've kept count correctly, the game I just finished was #67 in my time playing SOTM, and it also marks the moment at which I have played every hero exactly twelve times.  So it's time for more factoids from my datasheet.

* Absolute Zero still holds the death record - he's only survived to the end of the game four times.  However, he's been involved in victories for his team half the time; the record for game losses involving a single hero remains with Fanatic, who (despite my friend Chris's record of winning games with her) has only helped to win six of the games she's been in, and only one of those involved her dying - her other six failures were a gift she chose to share with the group.  At this point I'm forced to wonder if I'm subconsciously sabotaging her.  (Expatriette continues to be tied with Fanatic for second-most deaths, but has won the game once more while dying in the process.)

* On the other end of the spectrum, Nightmist continues to hold the best survival record, having only been incapacitated in one game.  She and Omnitron-X have both won all but one of the games they've played in!  (Omnix died in two of these victories, but I've also seen another player run him to good effect, while I'm the only player in my circle of IRL friends that has tried Nightmist.  This doesn't include members of the forum games crew in games that I wasn't involved in, of course, any more than it includes RL games from before I started playing.)  Visionary and Scholar have only ever actually lost the game once, dying 2 and 3 times respectively, but they have also each been involved in one game which was conceded as a loss, after they were the only hero who survived and had clearly no hope of achieving a turnaround (this is different from conceding a game just out of lack of desire to continue it, without recognizing it as a win or a loss).  Interestingly, Visionary's concession comes from the same game in which Nightmist died...all the deck-control both heroines wield wasn't enough to turn that game around.

* The Ennead is the only villain I have not fought at least three times.

* Plague Rat is the only villain who I have not played three heroes against.  Akash'Bhuta is the only one I haven't played four heroes against.  (Multiple five-hero games are still in my future.)

* Iron Legacy has beaten me three times.  Spite has frustrated me into a concession (a not-win/loss one, that is) once, but never actually incapped one of my heroes, nor has Plague Rat or Akash'Bhuta, all in exactly three games.  So IL has defeated all my heroes (except once the Scholar) in as many games as the other three have failed to kill even one.

* I have played in every environment six times, except for Rook City, Pike Industrial, the Time Cataclysm, and the Tomb of Anubis (the latter is the only one that remains at just four plays).  The Realm of Discord is the only one where I have lost three games, and abandoned a fourth in disgust; I have won only two games there, as well as two of the four in the Tomb, making IR clearly the site of my greatest frustrations.  The Final Wasteland is the safest place in the world as far as I can tell; uniquely among environments, I've never lost a game there, and only had one hero even incapped.

* Of the 91 possible combinations of two heroes, the only ones I have yet to see in a game involving myself are Mr. Fixer + Tempest (ironic, given that art has shown the latter two together on several occasions), Mr. Fixer + Bunker, Bunker + Scholar, Omnitron-X with either Haka or Wraith, Wraith + Chrono-Ranger, and Absolute Zero with either Argent Adept or Chrono-Ranger.  (I seem to be prone to repeating combinations with these specific heroes for some reason.)  In addition to these eight matches I haven't seen are eleven where I have not played both heroes, totaling 72 of the possible combinations which I have explored.  (The number of combinations of two- and three-hero groups with each other or with additional single heroes is...rather larger, and I won't be making significant headway on it anytime soon.)

Took most of a week off from playing SOTM, but last Friday and this Friday involved three more games between them.  My next game will be the 75th, not counting forum games that started but haven't finished.  As my heroes move into "played 14x each" status one by one, with the online games preparing to make that 15 for the two heroes involved, I updated my database again and began looking at new, interesting categories to put my heroes into.  Here are my observations.

* Absolute Zero has played 13 games and only survived to the end in 4 of them, making him my "dyingest" hero.  However, my "losingest" hero is Fanatic, who has only died 8 times, but only helped her team to win one of those games while incapacitated...thusly, half of her games were losses.  Tempest splits the difference; he's been incapped in half his games...however, he's only actually won six games, because he's the only hero with whom I've quit a game twice before he was killed (once by making a rules error which mandated that I forfeit the game, and once by my simply losing patience with the game and abandoning it without resolution).

* Nightmist died for the second time last night (it was the Advanced Ennead vs. five heroes, so a loss is hardly surprising, but it's particularly insulting that Nightmist was the very first casualty, not to mention that she partly caused the defeat by casting Oblivion twice while the heroes had no protection against the blast).  She is still the only hero to have sustained no more than two incaps, making her the "livingest" hero.  However, Omnitron-X holds the title of my "winningest" hero, having lost only one game, even if he didn't survive to see two of his team's victories.  (Scholar is almost tied with him, having only actually lost one game, but conceded another one as a near-stalemate, in which he was more likely to eventually lose due to a moment of bad luck.  In both cases, they've had 13 games and so might not preserve the title after their next..currently Nightmist and Omnitron are tied for highest number of games won, but Misty had one more game total, so the title defaults to Omnix unless he loses his next game.)

* Mr. Fixer has fought the most different villains (13 in 14 games...Matriarch was the only repeat, and that was on normal once and Advanced once), while Ra has faced the fewest (just 8 in 13 games; everyone else has had at least 10 different foes, so Ra's 14th outing cannot possibly remove this "most incomplete" status from him).

* Haka specializes in Advanced matches more than any other hero I've played...a whopping 8 of them!  He is tied with Bunker and Nightmist for the most villains fought on both regular and Advanced (3 apiece).  Fanatic is unique in having never fought a single villain on both difficulty modes (she's fought Warlord Voss twice, but both times on Advanced, and Iron Legacy twice, who I've only ever faced on regular...I'm beginning to suspect I know why she loses half her games).  On the other end of the spectrum, Tempest has faced advanced villains only three times (tied with Ra in this respect, except that Tempest has had one more game..so I will deliberately be making Ra's next game Advanced, and in fact I've decided that will happen tonight), making his mere six victories even more pathetic.  (I would characterize him as a strong hero, so this poor performance is tragic and puzzling.)

* Absolute Zero and the Scholar are closest to having visited every environment, with only three more to go.  I plan on deliberately resolving the tie tonight, probably in the Scholar's favor, just for flavor reasons (and to try and address AZ's uniquely terrible performance as compared to Mr. Rhodes's excellence).  Conversely, of the heroes who I've tended to play again and again in the same environment, Tempest takes the cake - 14 different games, all of them set in Insula Primalis, Megalopolis, the Block, Wagner Mars Base, Silver Gulch, or the Realm of Discord.  (Again, I'm beginning to suspect I know why he's been having a hard time.)

* After seven games each in the core set environments (and The Block), I have almost but not quite gotten every single hero to visit one of them.  I have personally played 15 different heroes in Wagner Mars as of last night, so one more game could make it a hat trick, even with only three heroes.  The Block is close to this status, except that one of the 15 heroes there was not played by me, but by another player during one of my games.  The Realm of Discord is the runner-up among environments I've visited five or six times, as I've seen 14 heroes there.

* It may not be a coincidence since I've played more games there period, and a lot of them with many heroes, and often against particularly deadly villains (I keep hoping that Meteor Storm will protect me, even though Villainous Weaponry is more likely).  But for the moment, Wagner Mars has killed more of my heroes than any other environment - twelve of them!  Rook City is the runner up, and could easily surpass it in one more game.  Realm of Discord is the one I appear to be worst in, with three defeats and a concession out of six total games, although Tomb of Anubis has also killed me three times in just five games.  The Final Wasteland remains my "happy place"; only Bunker has ever died there.  Ruins of Atlantis has also been good to me, with only one three-hero defeat; the Block and Megalopolis have the same won/loss ratio over 7 games, but have killed more heroes in the process.

* Visionary is the only hero who has played all 12 possible positions (excluding the Freedom Six game, which I have done once).

* Haka has never played second in turn order in his 14 games.  This was largely accidental - sometimes I couldn't remember that he was waiting for a chance at position 2, while other times I gave it to another hero who wanted it more.  I was uniquely stupid in setting up my game last night, as I could only remember one position I wanted to fill (Unity playing last in a 5er, and even there, I would have preferred to do 4th); had I checked my records, Fixer and Nightmist and Haka could all have crossed some positions off their todo list.

I am proud to announce that as of the 7th of this month, I have been involved in games featuring the nemesis of every villain which has one pre-Vengeance.  It took me 103 games to happen to have Fanatic meet Apostate, but the set is now complete, unless promo versions are counted separately - and even then, as of yesterday when I introduced Nightmist to Skinwalker Gloomy, I am missing only a Cosmotron vs. O-X game (having not done a full game against Cosmic Omnitron at all).

My 108-game series of "(almost) every villain exactly six times, in (almost) every Environment exactly nine times" is now complete except for an in-progress game on this forum, and so it's time to mention a few more stats...they're decreasing in relevance even as I'm decreasing in free time, so I'll make this brief.

* with 16 plays for Unity and Fanatic, 19 for Chrono-Ranger, Fixer, and all the male core-set heroes who don't wear power-armor, and 17 or 18 for each of the remaining heroes, Expatriette is by far my "dyingest" hero, having gotten incapacitated in 12 out of 18 games.  I really don't know what I'm doing wrong.  She also holds the title of "losingest", though not by as massive a margin - just 9 games.  Absolute Zero and Argent Adept are the runners-up in losingness, with 10 deaths each (Argent in one more total games than AZ), and Fanatic's low total game count is probably all that keeps her from equalling or exceeding Expat's loss count, having died nine times and only helped win one of those games.  Argent is also at 8 game losses, while Zero is tied with Tempest and Fixer for 7.

* Nightmist has died only three times, and each of these corresponded to a game loss; Wraith has 4 incaps and 4 losses in the same 18 games.  Scholar has been incapped four times, but only lost one of those games; however he has conceded two other games as losses while remaining active (once because of a rules snafu that made me abandon the game, and once because he was trapped in an indefinite stalemate which he would eventually lose due to having to reshuffle his deck).  Chrono-Ranger, Haka and Ra also have excellent win records, with only five games lost out of 19; Haka died in 7 of these games and the other two in 6.

* Haka and Tachyon have fought in every environment except Pike Industries; the Scholar has fought everywhere except in Rook City (which is also the one environment I haven't visited a ninth time, while Realm of Discord has gotten ten games due to an error in my recordkeeping).

* Visionary had played every possible position (first, second, third, fourth or fifth in a game with three, four, or five heroes) even before the Nemesis Challenge occurred (which I think was in January); she was joined in that accomplishment by Chrono-Ranger during the Challenge and by the Scholar earlier this month.

* Deviations from my six-games-per-villain schedule are as follows:  +1 game vs. Baron Blade, +1 vs. Spite, +2 vs. Gloomweaver (all of these due to promo games; the last SkinnyGloom battle is technically outside the 108-game series), while -1 vs. Akash'Bhuta, -1 vs. the Ennead, -1 vs. Iron Legacy, -1 vs. normal Spite, the yet-to-be-completed game against La Capitan, and one game which experimented with a PVP format and didn't include a villain at all.  It's ironic that Abby and the Ennead are two of my three favorite villains, but I never made quite enough time for plays against them, while I got seven games in against each of the lacking Baron and Spite, and a whopping eight versus the wimpy and awkward Gloomweaver (though this is largely due to my playing two games against him in sequence last night, with the victory over regular Gloomy being such a landslide that I proposed a sequel against his more difficult version).

* Despite the fact that I almost exclusively play him on Advanced, I have never seen regular Gloomweaver flip, and only in my first game did we beat him by destroying three Relics.  The rest of the time, even if melee or projectile damage is unavailable, he's easily beaten senseless without waiting around for the Relics to turn up, or risking a Vast Following returning them.

* All but one of my five games against Akash have been advanced, and that's likely to remain true in future games.  Conversely, I've fought the Chairman six times but only dared to go advanced once; the same is true of the Matriarch, but I'll be more likely to fix that in a future game.  Iron Legacy has also had only one advanced game, but that's out of five total, and for the moment the same is true of La Capitan, though a second advanced and sixth total game is pending.  For the remaining villains I have generally gone half-and-half, with Voss and Gloomy erring on the side of Advanced and Plague Rat on the not, and Spite and the Ennead have had five total games, two of them advanced.

* Ambuscade has been beaten in all six of my games against him, and Spite has also never beaten me, though he did elicit a concession due to a rule goof.  Iron Legacy and the Matriarch have each racked up four wins against me, with the Chairman, Dreamer, Miss Info and for the moment La Capitan all sitting at three (although last night's Chairman game might not have been a win if not for a rules snafu, and my first against Miss Info almost certainly wouldn't).  Citizen Dawn, Grand Warlord Voss, and the Ennead have two wins each against me, and Apostate has one win and a game that was scrapped out of impatience and confusion.  That leaves five villains who have yet to beat me twice, with all except Abby having had at least six chances.  Off the top of my head, Miss Info and the Ennead are the villains who I have always beaten on non-Advanced and never done so on Advanced, though this may be true of others that I haven't double-checked as yet (but probably not), and only in the Ennead's case am I fairly certain the victories were legitimate.

* Fun fact - in my four games against promo villains (not on advanced mode, but still), I have not had a hero incapacitated.  Of regular villains, only Spite is comparably ineffective at killing my guys, though of course that's over more than twice as many encounters.  Every villain except Spite has killed at least three of my heroes, while La Capitan holds the record for the most different heroes who have died against her while under my control, closely followed by Iron Legacy and the Dreamer.
